subject: Close-date drift: inventory, re-baseline options and escalation requested
messages:
From: Megan Li <megan.li@acmehealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Sat, 14 Apr 2028 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MAP draft & target close

Sofia —

Quick heads-up from procurement: our vendor review window just slipped because finance is closing Q1 books next week. That means the acceptance cadence we agreed in the MAP is at risk. Current internal signals point to the close moving from ~2028-05-20 to somewhere in early June unless we re-baseline.

Can you do a short inventory of the risks this creates for Redwood (tech eval, go-live gate, billing) and propose two concrete options (conservative re-baseline and compressed/accelerated path with trade-offs)? Procurement also asked for the SOC2 answers and the procurement form (attached).

I attached the MAP_v1.xlsx we were working from. I can loop in our legal if you send a proposed new close or an offer (pilot/credit) that would preserve the May cadence.

Thanks —
Megan Li
Sr. Program Manager, Acme Health
megan.li@acmehealth.com
Attachments: MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), procurement_request_form.pdf (form stub)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Megan Li <megan.li@acmehealth.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Sat, 14 Apr 2028 15:10:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MAP draft & target close

Megan —

Thanks for the flag. I ran a quick risk inventory and outlined two pragmatic paths below. I attached an updated MAP (MAP_v2.xlsx) and a lightweight risk_inventory.csv.

Summary of immediate impacts:
- Eval window: 2 weeks lost from the pre-scheduled in-person validation (impacts throughput of acceptance testing).
- Billing cutover: if close slips into a new billing period we need to reissue invoices and may need a short-term PO amendment.
- Resource hold: our Dedicated capacity hold expires 5/25; if the close slips we either extend the hold (cost) or re-allocate.

Options (pick one):
1) Conservative re-baseline (recommended if exec approval is uncertain)
   - New proposed close: 2028-06-12
   - Actions: extend Dedicated hold through 6/20 (customer pays incremental hold fee), compress acceptance by running parallel KV validation with two engineering tracks.
   - Trade-offs: higher short-term cost to Acme; preserves full acceptance testing.

2) Aggressive compression (if Acme wants to keep May 20)
   - Target close: 2028-05-20 (no change)
   - Offer: 2-week paid pilot (reduced scope), priority routing for Dedicated capacity, and a 20% credit on first-month usage if acceptance completes by 5/20.
   - Trade-offs: tighter acceptance window, higher risk of post-go-live issues; requires an SLA addendum.

Ask from Acme: confirm which path you want to pursue by Mon 2028-04-17 so we can lock resource schedules. If you need an exception on credits >20% we'll need executive approval on our side.

Regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
+1 (555) 312-0192
Attachments: MAP_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), risk_inventory.csv (CSV stub)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Apr 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Close-date drift: inventory, re-baseline options and escalation requested

Sofia —

I reviewed Sofia's two paths and recommend we prepare a contingency package to keep momentum. Suggested playbook:
- Offer accelerated eval lane: temporary Dedicated burst (2 GPUs) to run acceptance in parallel; estimated cost = incremental $6k/week.
- Credit package: up to 30% credit on month-1 if Acme signs a 12-month committed Dedicated term. Anything >20% needs Kim (Kimberly Park) sign-off.
- Legal: prepare a short SLA addendum and a mutually limited indemnity carve-out for the compressed acceptance path.

Draft note to Acme (suggested):
"We can support two paths: conservative re-baseline to 2028-06-12, or an accelerated May 20 close supported by a 2-week pilot and priority Dedicated capacity. For the accelerated path we will offer a usage credit of 20% (up to 30% pending exec approval) on the first month. Please confirm preferred path and whether legal should begin redlines."

If Sofia wants, I can draft the legal & commercial language for the HubSpot deal and the DocuSign wrapper.

-Jonas
Director, Customer Success
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

From: Megan Li <megan.li@acmehealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 16 Apr 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Close-date drift: inventory, re-baseline options and escalation requested

Sofia / team —

Procurement reviewed the two options. A few items:
- We need the SOC2 answers before anything that looks like a contractual exception. Attached SOC2-evidence-answers.pdf.
- Our legal will need the SLA addendum redline; they won't sign on a >20% commercial concession without exec approval.
- Given internal calendar constraints, Acme can commit to a hard decision window by 2028-04-20 but cannot commit to June 12 without an Exec-level approval on their side. Right now their target is June 8 if we choose to re-baseline.

Next steps from our side: we will escalate to our CIO for approval on credit >20% and confirm by 4/20. In the meantime please share the legal redline template and a DocuSign draft if possible.

Megan
Attachments: SOC2-evidence-answers.pdf, procurement_request_form.pdf

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Megan Li <megan.li@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Apr 2028 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: Acme Health MAP — credit approval and re-baseline decision window

Kim —

Quick escalation summary and ask:

Why: Acme Health's procurement window slipped and they have signaled a potential move of our close from 2028-05-20 to early June. They are willing to decide by 2028-04-20 but need an exec-level confirmation from our side for any credit >20%.

What we propose: two options we can present to Acme (they pick one):
  A) Re-baseline to 2028-06-08 (Acme pref), extend Dedicated hold (customer pays incremental hold fee).
  B) Hold 2028-05-20 with an accelerated 2-week pilot + priority Dedicated capacity; commercial credit = 20% (can offer up to 30% with exec approval).

Commercial ask: authorization to offer up to 30% credit on month-1 usage if Acme signs a 12-month committed Dedicated term. This would be contingent on an SLA addendum and an abbreviated acceptance scope.

Operational notes: HubSpot deal ACME-2028-07 is updated with MAP_v2; DocuSign draft is ready here: https://www.docusign.net/ACME-2028-07-draft. SOC2 answers and procurement form are attached.

If you can greenlight up to 30% credit (or confirm 20% hard cap), I'll send the contingency package and the suggested language to Acme and move the redlines to DocuSign. They asked for a decision by 4/20 to keep momentum.

Thanks,
Sofia
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Attachments: MAP_v2.xlsx, risk_inventory.csv, SOC2-evidence-answers.pdf
